metadata.domain: Autonomous Driving Platform / ADAS / Automotive Electronics

evidence.trl_pathway: T01 (TRL 6→target in ~2 years) and T08 (TRL 5→target in 2 years) are moderately aggressive but plausible; T03 (TRL 7) scheduled for zero development duration (2030-Q1 to 2030-Q1) is a red flag indicating no meaningful development window was allocated.
evidence.strategic_fidelity: The portfolio includes mid-to-high TRL technologies (TRL 5-7) with a declared 기술선도 strategy, which ideally targets lower-TRL exploratory technologies; the selection of relatively mature technologies like Steer-by-Wire (TRL 7) weakens the technology leadership narrative, though sensor fusion and 3D pose estimation provide some R&D depth.
evidence.competitive_awareness: All three technologies (multi-sensor fusion, 3D pose estimation, steer-by-wire) are clearly within the autonomous driving/ADAS domain, demonstrating strong domain fit; the dependency chain (T01→T08→T03) reflects a logical technology stack building toward higher-level autonomous control.
evidence.market_timing: Two of three technologies (T08 and T03) complete more than 2 years after their respective market booms (2.25yr and 2.0yr late), and even T01 misses the optimal 기술선도 preemption window by completing 0.75 years after boom rather than 1-2 years before; systematic late completion undermines competitive positioning.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: The selected technologies are plausibly in convergence zones for autonomous driving (sensor fusion and pose estimation show strong patent and market activity), but the roadmap provides no explicit evidence of deliberate convergence-zone analysis; the selection appears driven more by dependency logic than convergence intelligence.

strengths: All technologies are strictly within the autonomous driving/ADAS domain, ensuring competitive positioning leverage from existing expertise
Dependency chain is logically structured and violation-free, building foundational sensing capabilities before higher-level control
weaknesses: Systematic late market timing — two technologies complete 2+ years after boom windows, largely negating any technology leadership advantage
Steer-by-Wire (TRL 7) has zero development duration allocated (same start and end quarter), making it effectively a phantom roadmap entry
missing_technologies: Low-TRL AI-based end-to-end autonomous driving stack (TRL 2-4) to credibly anchor a 기술선도 strategy
LiDAR point cloud deep learning processing to complement the sensor fusion camera system
V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) communication technology for next-generation ADAS competitive differentiation
investment_issues: T03 (Steer-by-Wire) is classified as 'High' tier despite being the terminal dependency in the chain — if upstream technologies are delayed, this investment yields no return
Budget is fully exhausted (100% utilization) with only 3 technologies, leaving no contingency for timeline slippage or emerging competitive threats
Investing heavily in TRL 7 Steer-by-Wire as a 기술선도 play is misaligned — mature technologies rarely yield technology leadership premiums
timing_issues: 3D Pose Estimation System completes in 2030-Q1 but market boom is 2027-Q4 — 2.25 years late, missing the peak market window entirely
Steer-by-Wire Control completes in 2030-Q1 but market boom is 2028-Q1 — exactly 2 years late, arriving in a post-peak market
For 기술선도, technologies should ideally complete 1-2 years BEFORE boom; instead all technologies complete at or after boom dates
